clue.text: Sanctioned wretch provided with makeshift bomb

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a wretch
if means provided that
IED, an improvised explosive device

explanation.surface: A villain is officially approved and handed a home-made bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty or decision is to give it formal approval, so ratified is a synonym of sanctioned.

clue.text: Rapidly turn firearm, increasing core volume?

indicators.note: increasing core means the middle of the word is enlarged by putting a letter in it

parts.note: a rifle is a firearm
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud volume

explanation.surface: Someone rapidly swings a gun round, turning up the sound in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Adding another F beside the F in the middle of RIFLE gives the doubled letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To riffle through pages or cards is to flick through them quickly.

clue.text: Tory's beginning to irritate Speaker

indicators.note: beginning means only the opening letter of Tory is used

parts.note: annoy means irritate

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician starts to get on the nerves of the Commons Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker suggests the chair of the House of Commons, but it is a loudspeaker; Tannoy is a British brand of public-address system.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tannoy is a public-address loudspeaker system, the brand name used generically in Britain.

clue.text: Last five crackers for Christmas, perhaps

definitions.note: perhaps signals that Christmas is an example of the answer

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: The final five Christmas crackers are left for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackers look like part of the Christmas scene but signal the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is a religious holiday and celebration, so it is one example of a festival.

clue.text: Regularly test music case

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A music case that is checked at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Briefly coming back to tour a state

indicators.note: to tour something is to go around it, so the reversed letters surround the A
back says the shortened word is read in the opposite direction
briefly tells us to cut the word short, dropping its last letter

parts.note: advent means a coming or arrival

explanation.surface: A short note about returning to travel round some state.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVENT (coming) loses its last letter to give ADVEN, which 'back' turns into NEVDA; that goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: Motor missing centre, needing to be replaced

indicators.note: to be replaced means the remaining letters are put back in a different arrangement
missing centre means the middle letter of needing is taken away

explanation.surface: An engine short of its central part has to be swapped for a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEDING loses its centre D to give NEEING, which 'to be replaced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a machine that produces motion, i.e. a motor.

clue.text: Counterpart with hands?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something comparable to another, a counterpart
second meaning: an ... watch or clock shows time with hands rather than digits

explanation.walkthrough: 'With hands' suggests a person, but it describes a clock face as opposed to a digital display.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogue means both a parallel equivalent and, of a timepiece, displaying time with moving pointers.

clue.text: Almighty deed, changing cats for dogs — all tailless

indicators.note: changing means the remaining letters are altered into a fresh order
tailless means each of the three words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Something miraculous happens: cats turn into dogs, and none have tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All tailless' cuts CATS, FOR and DOGS to CAT, FO and DOG; 'changing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of God is an event outside human control, such as a natural disaster, attributed to the Almighty.

clue.text: Chinese order of cooked fish, e.g. skinned tuna

indicators.note: cooked means the assembled letters are prepared into a new arrangement

parts.note: the abbreviation for 'for example', taken as its letters

indicators.note: skinned means the outer layer of the word tuna is stripped, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A Chinese restaurant order of fish dishes, such as tuna with the skin removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The food surface points to a takeaway order, but 'Chinese order' is the definition. Rearrange FISH, EG and UN (tuna without its outer letters).
explanation.definitionFit: Feng shui is the Chinese system for ordering and arranging a space in harmony with its surroundings.

clue.text: Inside of gulag has tourists stunned

indicators.note: inside of says the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Visitors are shocked by what a Soviet labour camp contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast describes someone struck with horror or amazement, a near-synonym of stunned.

clue.text: A horse/sheep mix-up

parts.note: a nag is a horse, usually an old one
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A cross between a horse and a sheep, an odd hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a word made by jumbling the letters of another, a mix-up of letters.

clue.text: Ladies perhaps hide, forgoing second chance

parts.note: the Ladies is a women's toilet, and loo is British slang for any toilet

indicators.note: forgoing means going without, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: Women, it seems, conceal something and pass up a second opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: A loo is a toilet, so 'Ladies' (the women's toilet) is an example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-in is an informal British term for an opportunity to take part, i.e. a chance.

clue.text: Occasionally fond of an oddball

indicators.note: an oddball is strange or eccentric, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone is now and then fond of an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: On and off is an idiom for intermittently, happening at irregular intervals rather than constantly.

clue.text: Sorry criminal has identified missing head

indicators.note: criminal means wrong, so these letters are set out in a wrong order
missing head means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them

explanation.surface: A remorseful crook has fingered someone but lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun for a crook; it is an adjective making an anagram of HAS. NAMED without its head gives AMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling guilt or embarrassment, the regretful sense of sorry.

clue.text: Tube fare — you've got nothing without it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: food in the shape of a tube, a cased length of minced meat
second meaning: the British idiom 'not a ...' means nothing at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube fare' suggests the price of a London Underground ticket, but fare here is food. 'Not a sausage' is British slang for nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger, the British word for this meat product, is tubular food, and the idiom 'not a sausage' means nothing.

clue.text: Regret turning over continental bread

indicators.note: turning means the word for regret is read back to front

parts.note: to rue is to regret
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about flipping European loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' reads as one phrase but splits: 'turning' acts on RUE, and 'over' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the euro is the currency of much of continental Europe.

clue.text: Endless petitions about record that's typically American

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase; the answer is used in 'as American as apple pie'

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes around the record
endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: applies, as a noun plural sense: applications, formal requests or petitions
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Constant appeals about a record that is quintessentially American.
explanation.walkthrough: APPLIES (requests) loses its end to give APPLIE, which goes about EP. The answer comes from the saying 'as American as apple pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is the dessert proverbially seen as the most American thing, hence a byword for wholesome Americana.

clue.text: Scattered rice lost in part of cathedral

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters are dispersed into a new order

explanation.surface: Wedding rice thrown about has gone missing in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered walkway around a courtyard, a feature of many cathedrals and monasteries.

clue.text: Ordnance Survey spread out in Barnes & Noble

indicators.note: spread out means the two map letters are dispersed among the bookseller's name to make a new arrangement

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for the Ordnance Survey, Britain's mapping agency
the name is used as written, its letters joining the pool

explanation.surface: Maps are laid out in the Barnes & Noble bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The bookseller's name suggests a whole phrase, but 'Noble' is the definition. O and S are spread out separately into BARNES, as BAR-O-NE-S-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a woman holding the rank of baron, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Look after river sport

indicators.note: after places the word for look behind the river

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to tend a stream and play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as one phrase meaning tend, but 'after' is the ordering signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team game played on horseback with long mallets, so it is an example of a sport.

clue.text: British fruit and nuts

parts.note: ananas is another name for the pineapple

explanation.surface: A list of homegrown fruit and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit and nuts' looks like a snack list; nuts is the definition, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bananas is slang for going mad, so bananas means crazy, the slang sense of nuts.

clue.text: Support for driver with trimmed wheel that's funny

parts.note: a tee holds the golf ball for a shot with a driver

indicators.note: trimmed means the word wheel has its edges cut off, front and back

explanation.surface: A golf tee and a cut-down wheel make a comic combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist with a wheel, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is an interjection imitating a giggle, the response to something amusing.

clue.text: I enjoy drugs and rock and roll, primarily

definitions.note: a self-description standing for the noun naming such a person

parts.note: a stone is a piece of rock

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of roll is used

explanation.surface: A self-confessed fan of drugs and rock and roll speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a first-person description: the person saying it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoner is slang for a person who regularly uses cannabis or other drugs.

clue.text: Article in French newspaper that is socialist

parts.note: le is the French definite article
the FT is the Financial Times
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece in a French paper that has left-wing views.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftie is an informal term for someone holding left-wing politics, such as a socialist.

clue.text: Was waiter's duck covered in low-calorie wine?

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the past tense, matching the answer

indicators.note: covered in means the zero letter is wrapped inside the word for low-calorie

parts.note: lite is the advertising spelling of light, meaning low in calories
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the shape of O
red is a colour of wine

explanation.surface: A question about whether a waiter's duck was served smothered in diet wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and links the definition to the wordplay; the waiter is not serving at table but waiting about.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang around idly, so someone who loitered was one who waited about.

clue.text: Dickie Bird initially backed English one and two

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of bird is used
backed means the following words are read in reverse order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
the number word itself

explanation.surface: Dickie Bird, the famous English cricket umpire, recalled as he started out with one and two.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickie Bird was a well-known English cricket umpire; here 'Dickie' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dickie bow, or dicky, is British slang for the knotted neckwear worn with evening dress.

clue.text: Retreat from short Scottish landowner

indicators.note: short means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A retreat from a minor Scottish estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a hidden den or hideaway, a place one withdraws to, as a retreat.

clue.text: Course covering constant alongside unknown variable

indicators.note: covering means the path goes over and around the constant

parts.note: a path is a course or route
c is the symbol for a constant, e.g. the speed of light
y is a conventional algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A maths course covers a constant next to an unknown variable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown variable' reads as the algebraic phrase, but 'variable' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchy means uneven in quality or inconsistent, which is what variable means of performance or weather.

clue.text: Light brown mist swirling until one's lost

parts.note: haze is a light mist

indicators.note: swirling means the remaining letters are churned into a new order
lost means that letter goes missing from the word until

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A pale brown fog swirls about until someone loses their way.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I from UNTIL to leave UNTL, which 'swirling' rearranges to LNUT, after HAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is the colour of the ripe nut, a light brown, so the nut's name serves as the colour.

clue.text: Lake taken in by extremely eager stranger

indicators.note: taken in by means the lake's name sits inside the outer letters
extremely means taking the extreme letters, first and last, of eager

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A lake gets swallowed up by a very keen outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for an outsider; here it is the comparative adjective, more strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerier is the comparative of eerie, meaning more uncanny or weird, i.e. stranger.

clue.text: Keep quiet about aid

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
re means about or concerning
to serve is to help or aid

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their mouth shut about the help they gave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep quiet' reads as one phrase; 'Keep' alone is the definition and 'quiet' is P.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to keep something safe or maintain it, a direct synonym.
